items.evidence: The second step reloads the draft's address (draft-deletion.spec.ts line 77 in the diff) and asserts the not-found screen with no status-info (lines 78-80). That would fail if the server never deleted the draft.
Both criteria are asserted: the drafts-list URL and the create-draft button (lines 71-73), and the not-found screen at the deleted draft's address (lines 77-81).

The new locators (moreActionsButton, deleteMenuItem, notFoundMessage, goBackToDashboardButton) and delete() are added to DraftOrderPage, which had none of them. The spec reuses the page object's existing dialog, createDraftButton and statusInfo.
There are no fixed waits; delete() waits with waitForURL and web-first assertions.
The spec imports test from ../../fixtures/test.ts, has no parallel() tag, and writes nothing to the cache or the dumps.

Locators use test ids or role and name. The dialog's submit is scoped to the dialog, and show-more-button is scoped to page-header. getByText is used only for the not-found screen, which has no test id.
The draft is started with the existing DraftOrderPage.create flow; nothing is set up through the API.
No ids are hard-coded: the draft URL is read from page.url() after creation. The channel comes from CHANNEL.name.
The test uses the default admin stored session, with no UI sign-in and no credentials in the spec; the ticket names no specific permission.
The spec is at e2e/tests/orders/draft-deletion.spec.ts, and typecheck.txt reports exit 0 with no errors.
The spec defines no locators or multi-step UI actions inline; all of them live on DraftOrderPage.
The new members are readonly fields initialised from this.page, and the existing constructor(readonly page: Page) {} is kept.
The spec has // Arrange and // Act & Assert comments (lines 58 and 68).
It is one test with a test.step for each stage.
The title 'Staff delete a draft order from its menu after confirming #e2e' describes the behaviour and carries the #e2e tag.
A header comment explains what the spec covers and why (lines 50-54).
All UI assertions are web-first. The pathname check on page.url() is a precondition on a captured value, not page text.
The spec uses ORDERS_SCENARIO and CHANNEL.name from the scenario; no money is compared.
There is no cleanup code and there are no unique names.
There are no per-test timeouts, retries, networkidle or waitForLoadState.
Relative imports keep the .ts extension, and test/expect come only from the fixture.
There is no any, no cast and no gql call.
The comments explain reasons: the menu test id that is never rendered, the misleading 'Cancel order' label, the missing test ids on the not-found screen, and why the URL is read rather than built.

structured_output.summary: Submission a53e5c32 meets all 23 checklist items (B1–B10, M1–M13); nothing fails. The spec deletes the draft through new methods on DraftOrderPage, the existing page object. It then proves the deletion happened on the server by reopening the draft's address and checking for the not-found screen. Both acceptance criteria are asserted, and typecheck.txt reports exit 0 with no errors. The diff also adds a planning note, specs/draft-order-deletion.md. No checklist item covers it, so it does not affect any verdict.
